contracts.blurb: Neighbourhood shops want fresh ugu, cucumbers and a few yam tubers.
A supermarket chain needs washed, graded produce on the shelf by 7 AM.
Hotel kitchens and party caterers order rice and plantain every week.
Trailer loads of yam and local rice for depots in other states.
Cross-border trucks carry Naija yam and rice down the coast road.
A cool container of yam every week for diaspora shops abroad.

belt.name: Crate Roller Conveyor
belt.blurb: Rolls washed, sorted produce from the barn straight to the counter.

auto.name: Farm Tractor & Harvester
auto.blurb: Ridges, plants and harvests the plots without waiting for farmhands.

pack.name: Wash & Grade Pack Line
pack.blurb: Washes, sorts by size, bags and labels produce to export standard.

milestones.title: First Produce Depot
milestones.blurb: A second selling point in Lagos. Baba Tunde is no longer a one-market man.

milestones.title: Lagos Market Ring
milestones.blurb: Five depots around Lagos share one truck route, so nothing sits and spoils.

milestones.title: Farmer Aggregator
milestones.blurb: You now buy from outgrower farmers at the farm gate, not only your own plots.

milestones.title: South-West Food Chain
milestones.blurb: Depots in Ogun, Oyo and Ondo sit close to the yam and plantain farms.

milestones.title: Cold Room Network
milestones.blurb: Solar cold rooms at every hub keep ugu and cucumbers fresh for days, not hours.

milestones.title: Nationwide Food Basket
milestones.blurb: From Benue yam belt to Kano rice mills, your trailers cover every region.

milestones.title: ECOWAS Produce Corridor
milestones.blurb: Depots open along the coast in Cotonou, Lomé and Accra. Border papers in order.

milestones.title: Plantain Flour Factory
milestones.blurb: Unsold plantain and yam now become flour and chips. Waste turns to profit.

milestones.title: Diaspora Shelf Space
milestones.blurb: Your labelled yam boxes sit in African stores from London to Houston.

milestones.title: Global Agro Empire
milestones.blurb: 500 depots on three continents. The world eats from Baba Tunde's farm.

events.name: New Yam Season
events.text: Fresh new yam just arrived. Everybody wants pounded yam today.

events.name: Heavy Rain on Farm Road
events.text: The farm road is all mud. Produce trucks are crawling in late.

events.name: Owambe Weekend
events.text: Party caterers are buying rice and plantain in bulk for weddings.

events.name: Plantain Scarcity
events.text: Dry season cut the plantain harvest. Buyers pay more per bunch.

events.name: Hot Sun Spoils Ugu
events.text: Heat wilted a batch of ugu and cucumbers. You must replace the stock.

events.name: Glut in the Market
events.text: Every trader has yam today. Customers are spread thin.

events.name: Agro Fair Prize
events.text: Your giant yam tuber won best produce at the state agro fair!

events.name: Cool Harmattan Morning
events.text: Cool breeze, no sweat. The farmhands are harvesting at double pace.

research.claim: Nigeria grows over 60% of the world's yams, yet Ghana supplies more than 90% of West Africa's yam exports and 20-30% of export volume arrives rotten.
After Nigeria's 2017 yam export launch at a Lagos container terminal, a UK importer said he expected at least one container of yams from Nigeria every week.
About half of Nigeria's fresh fruit and vegetables spoil before reaching consumers, and solar walk-in cold rooms rent space per 20 kg crate per day to farmers and traders.
Plantain post-harvest loss in Nigeria is about 30%, and processing into flour and snacks (some exported to Europe and the US) reduces it; main harvest is August to December.
